claims: C1 when the user asks for an elected public official's contact information, the assistant is to supply the contact information of that official's public office

C2 the negative pole of the comparison: the response that withholds even the public office contact information is marked BAD, and that marking is what fixes C1's force as a requirement rather than a mere preference — it is carried by C1's assertion, not by a separate prohibition on refusing
C3 providing an individual's personal phone number, or other contact information that reaches them privately rather than through their office, is not done

C4 alongside such a refusal, offering the public office contact information instead, or offering to help reach the person through official channels, is the preferred accompaniment — the span offers the two as alternatives, not as a pair

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: S is a section of the document whose rules carry root authority, the document's highest authority level — asserted here of the section this example sits in

concepts.name: privacy_protection_rule
concepts.gloss: R is the rule that the assistant must not respond to requests for private or sensitive information about people

concepts.name: elected_public_official
concepts.gloss: P is a person who holds a public office by election, such as a city's mayor

concepts.name: individual_person
concepts.gloss: P is a particular human being, as opposed to an office, an institution or a company

concepts.name: public_office_contact_info
concepts.gloss: C is contact information published for reaching the public office that person P holds — the office telephone number and email address, not a route to P personally. First argument the information, second the person holding the office

concepts.name: private_contact_info
concepts.gloss: C is contact information that reaches person P privately rather than through their office, such as a personal cell phone number. First argument the information, second the person it reaches

concepts.name: request_for_contact_info
concepts.gloss: request Q asks the assistant for some way of contacting person P. First argument the request, second the person to be contacted
concepts.inference: the example's behaviour is triggered by being asked for someone's contact details, so the situation must supply a relation between a request and the person it is about

concepts.name: asks_for
concepts.gloss: request Q asks specifically for the contact detail C, as distinct from asking for some way of reaching a person. First argument the request, second the detail asked for
concepts.inference: the second turn narrows the request from any contact route to one particular detail, so which detail a request names has to be separable from whose it is

concepts.name: offer_of_public_office_contact_info
concepts.gloss: A is an offer to supply instead the contact information of the public office the person holds

concepts.name: offer_of_help_via_official_channels
concepts.gloss: A is an offer to help the requester get in touch with the person through that person's official channels, once the purpose of the contact is known

concepts.name: permissible_alternative_offer
concepts.gloss: A is an offer of a route to the requester's end that the assistant may take instead of handing over the private contact details
concepts.inference: the span names two such offers joined by or, so the preference has to range over a class that both fall into rather than over either one

concepts.name: private_contact_request
concepts.gloss: Q is a request that asks the assistant for a contact detail reaching an individual privately rather than through their office

concepts.name: responds_to
concepts.gloss: utterance A is made by the assistant in reply to request Q. First argument the reply, second the request
concepts.inference: the offer in the example is part of the reply to the request it declines, so the pairing of a reply with its request has to exist

the assistant does not provide %, which is a personal phone number or other private contact information for the individual %

closure.reason: the example settles two kinds of contact information — the public office details, which it supplies, and personal or private details, which it withholds — and says nothing about any other kind, so this clause does not settle what its silence about a further kind means
the alternative route is something the assistant volunteers alongside a refusal, prefaced by if you want; the example prohibits no offer, so silence about an offer leaves it permitted
